subject: Physics
title: Nuclei
summary: A nucleus is made of protons (Z) and neutrons (N); A = Z + N is the mass number. Its size grows as A^{1/3}, so every nucleus has almost the same density (~2.3 × 10¹⁷ kg/m³).
A nucleus weighs LESS than its separate protons and neutrons. This missing mass (mass defect) becomes binding energy through E = mc² — the energy needed to break the nucleus apart.

Binding energy per nucleon (BE/A) measures stability. It is highest (~8.8 MeV) near A ≈ 56 (iron). That is why splitting a heavy nucleus (fission) and joining light nuclei (fusion) both release energy.
The nuclear force is very strong, short-range (~2–3 fm), charge-independent and attractive (repulsive only at very short distances).

formulas.name: Notation and composition
formulas.formula: ᴬ_Z X:  Z = protons,  N = A − Z = neutrons

formulas.name: Nuclear radius
formulas.formula: R = R₀ A^{1/3},   R₀ ≈ 1.2 fm (1 fm = 10⁻¹⁵ m)
formulas.mistake: R ∝ A^{1/3}, but volume ∝ A — don't mix them up.

formulas.name: Nuclear density
formulas.formula: ρ = 3 m_u / (4π R₀³) ≈ 2.3 × 10¹⁷ kg/m³  (independent of A)
formulas.note: Every nucleus has the same density — it does not change with A.

formulas.name: Atomic mass unit
formulas.formula: 1 u = 1/12 × (mass of a ¹²C atom) = 1.66 × 10⁻²⁷ kg ≡ 931.5 MeV/c²

formulas.name: Mass–energy relation
formulas.mistake: c = 3 × 10⁸ m/s and mass in kg — don't use grams.

formulas.name: Mass defect
formulas.formula: Δm = [Z m_p + (A − Z) m_n] − M_nucleus   (with atomic masses, use m_H instead of m_p)
formulas.when: How much mass 'disappears' when a nucleus forms.
formulas.note: Atomic masses include electrons — keep the same convention on both sides.

formulas.name: Binding energy
formulas.when: Energy needed to break the nucleus completely.

formulas.name: Binding energy per nucleon
formulas.formula: BE/A;   peak ≈ 8.8 MeV near A ≈ 56;   ≈ 8 MeV for 30 < A < 170
formulas.mistake: Higher BE/A = more stable — not the higher total BE.

formulas.name: Q-value of a reaction
formulas.formula: Q = (Σ m_reactants − Σ m_products) c² = Σ BE_products − Σ BE_reactants

formulas.name: Nuclear fission
formulas.note: About 200 MeV per fission, i.e. ~0.9 MeV per nucleon.

formulas.name: Nuclear fusion
formulas.formula: Sun: 4 ¹H → ⁴He + 2e⁺ + 2ν + 26.7 MeV;   ²H + ²H → ³He + n + 3.27 MeV
formulas.note: Needs a very high temperature (~10⁷ K) to overcome Coulomb repulsion.

examples.title: Size of a nucleus
examples.problem: Radius of ²⁷Al? How many times larger is ¹²⁵Te?

examples.title: Nuclear density
examples.problem: Find the density of nuclear matter (m_u = 1.66 × 10⁻²⁷ kg, R₀ = 1.2 fm).
examples.solution: ρ = A m_u / (4/3 π R₀³ A) = 3 m_u/(4πR₀³) ≈ 2.3 × 10¹⁷ kg/m³ — about 10¹⁴ times denser than water, and independent of A.

examples.title: Binding energy of helium-4
examples.problem: m(¹H) = 1.007825 u, m_n = 1.008665 u, m(⁴He atom) = 4.002603 u. Find BE and BE/A.

examples.title: Energy in 1 g of mass
examples.problem: If 1 g of mass were fully converted into energy?
examples.solution: E = mc² = 10⁻³ × (3 × 10⁸)² = 9.0 × 10¹³ J — enough electricity for a large city for days.

examples.title: Fission of 1 kg of U-235
examples.problem: Each fission gives 200 MeV. Energy from 1 kg of ²³⁵U?

examples.title: Q-value of D–D fusion
examples.problem: ²H = 2.014102 u, ³He = 3.016029 u, n = 1.008665 u. Find Q for ²H + ²H → ³He + n.

examples.title: Fission energy from BE/A
examples.problem: A nucleus with A = 240 (BE/A = 7.6 MeV) splits into two nuclei with A = 120 (BE/A = 8.5 MeV). Energy released?

topics.title: What a nucleus is made of
topics.explain: Protons + neutrons = nucleons. Atoms with the same Z but different A (¹H, ²H, ³H) behave the same chemically. A nucleus is ~fm (10⁻¹⁵ m) across, an atom ~Å (10⁻¹⁰ m) — the atom is ~10⁵ times bigger.

topics.title: Atomic masses
topics.explain: Atomic masses are measured in u (¹²C = exactly 12 u). They are not whole numbers — that small difference is the key to mass defect.

topics.title: From mass defect to binding energy
topics.explain: When nucleons join, a little mass is released as energy. Supply that energy back and the nucleus breaks apart. Hence BE = Δm c².

topics.title: The BE/A curve
topics.explain: Small A: BE/A rises quickly (He-4 is a local peak). Maximum ~8.8 MeV at A ≈ 56 (Fe). Large A: falls slowly (U ~7.6 MeV). Meaning: middle nuclei are the most stable; heavy nuclei release energy by fission, light ones by fusion.

topics.title: Properties of the nuclear force
topics.explain: The strongest force (~100 times Coulomb), very short range (~2–3 fm), the same for p-p, n-n and p-n (charge-independent), and saturating (each nucleon bonds only with its neighbours) — which is why BE/A is roughly constant.

topics.title: Fission and the chain reaction
topics.explain: A slow neutron splits ²³⁵U, releasing 2–3 new neutrons that cause more fissions. Controlled chain reaction = nuclear reactor (the moderator slows neutrons; control rods of Cd/B absorb them). Uncontrolled = atom bomb.

topics.title: Fusion and the stars
topics.explain: Light nuclei join into a heavier one — more energy per unit mass than fission. Bringing positive nuclei close needs enormous heat (thermonuclear). The Sun shines by fusing hydrogen into helium.

topics.title: Syllabus note
topics.explain: Radioactivity (properties of alpha, beta, gamma, the decay law, half-life) and the definitions of isotopes/isobars/isotones have been removed from the current (revised in 2024) JEE Main and NEET syllabus. This chapter focuses on size, density, mass defect, binding energy, the BE/A curve, fission and fusion.
